_meta.engine_compatibility: filter_engine.py v14.1 / config.py v13.1 / database.py v9.0 / monitors.py v9.7 / main.py v13.1
_meta.architecture: NLP Pipeline — Tokenization → Entity Extraction → Negation Analysis → Dependency Analysis → Distance Scoring → Ad Detection → Confidence Engine → Explainability
design_principles: Template-driven generation AND a curated static high_confidence_boost_patterns list co-exist: templates cover combinatorial coverage, the static list covers precise, high-value phrases that are not natural template combinations
Every lexicon entry has ONE canonical form
Ad detection: strong_provider = immediate reject, weak_provider requires 3+ commercial signals
Negation is clause-based with explicit boundaries
Token distance modifies score; message length modifies confidence
English academic terms receive lower weight unless accompanied by Arabic intent verb
Auto-learning disabled; human approval required for feedback integration

CRITICAL: every keyword string used for trie matching MUST already be in normalized form (no أ/إ/آ/ة/ى/ئ/ؤ). filter_engine.py normalizes INPUT text via _normalize_arabic() before searching the tries, but keyword entries loaded from this file are used AS-IS, with no normalization applied on the keywords side.

CRITICAL (v15.2, new finding): the same AS-IS rule applies to English tokens. _clean() lower-cases the INPUT text before every trie search, but keyword entries are matched as-is with no case-folding on the keywords side. Any keyword entry containing an uppercase Latin character (e.g. the previous 'PowerPoint', 'Excel', 'Mind Map') can never match lower-cased input and is silently dead weight — identical failure class to the Arabic-normalization bug, just for Latin script. Every English keyword in this file is now lower-case only (see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 1).

CRITICAL (v15.2, new finding): a message-sharing link is not inherently commercial. ad_blockers previously hard-blocked generic 'http://'/'https://'/'www.' prefixes and academic file-sharing domains (Google Drive/Docs, YouTube, Dropbox, OneDrive) that students routinely paste when sharing lecture files or assignment briefs. Because ad_blocker_trie is an early short-circuit in analyze() (any match -> immediate 'ignore'), this was silently rejecting legitimate academic messages that happened to include a file link. ad_blockers is now scoped to redirect/shortener/social/messaging-app domains only (see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 2).

IMPORTANT (v15.2): this file's design-target confidence thresholds are now kept in sync with config.py's actual runtime defaults (CONFIDENCE_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD=0.65 / CONFIDENCE_REVIEW_THRESHOLD=0.40) instead of documenting an aspirational 0.78/0.55 pair the runtime never applied. If accounts.env is ever changed to override those two env vars, confidence_thresholds_design_target below must be updated in the same change (see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 3).

KNOWN LIMITATION (documented, not fixable from this file alone): resolution_trie.search_first() returns a match anywhere in the message and, at score>=0.7, short-circuits the whole message to 'ignore' — there is no clause-level scoping in filter_engine.py v14.1. A message that both resolves an old request and raises a new one in the same text (e.g. 'لقيت حل للواجب لكن عندي تقرير ثاني محتاج مساعدة فيه') will currently be mis-classified as ignore. Mitigated here by keeping resolution_phrases as long, low-ambiguity exact phrases rather than short generic ones, but a real fix requires clause-level resolution detection in filter_engine.py (tracked for a future engine version, not a data-only fix).

KNOWN LIMITATION (documented): template_boost is a fixed +0.25 confidence add-on hard-coded in filter_engine.py's analyze() and is NOT gated on academic_object/university_context presence at the engine level. Generic template combinations (e.g. '<availability> <person>' -> 'مين يساعد') can therefore earn the same +0.25 boost whether or not the message is academic. Mitigated here by keeping the template word banks (person/availability/action/expert) oriented toward help-seeking phrasing rather than fully generic terms, but true context-gating requires an engine change (recommended follow-up, not implemented in this data file).

test_cases.*.text are deliberately left in natural/raw Arabic spelling (with ة, hamzas, etc.) because they represent simulated RAW user input that itself passes through the normalization pipeline during a test run — normalizing them here would test something other than production behavior.

fuzzy_matching._note: v15.2: previously only_for=[] meant fuzzy matching (edit distance <= 2) was effectively unscoped across the entire vocabulary — high risk of false positives in Arabic, where many unrelated short roots differ by 1-2 characters (e.g. واجب/واجه, بحث/بحه, مقرر/مقر). Scoped to a short, high-value list and tightened edit distance to match CFG.FUZZY_MAX_EDIT_DISTANCE's own default (1, not 2) and a longer minimum token length so short/common words are never fuzzy-matched.

confidence_thresholds_design_target._note: v15.2: aligned to the ACTUAL runtime defaults from config.py (CFG.CONFIDENCE_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD=0.65, CFG.CONFIDENCE_REVIEW_THRESHOLD=0.40) instead of the previous aspirational 0.78/0.55 pair, which the runtime never enforced (env-var default mismatch — see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 3). If these env vars are changed in accounts.env, update this block in the same change so the file never again documents a target the runtime doesn't apply.

fixes_changelog: == v15.2 (this pass) — engineering-audit hardening ==

1) [P0-fixable-in-data] English case-folding bug: filter_engine.py's _clean() lower-cases INPUT text but keyword entries are matched AS-IS with no case-folding applied on the keyword side (same failure class as the Arabic-normalization issue, documented in v15.1's item 6, just for Latin script). 'PowerPoint' -> 'powerpoint', 'Excel' -> 'excel' (all occurrences), 'Mind Map' -> 'mind map', 'Concept Map' -> 'concept map' in high_confidence_boost_patterns.patterns, which were previously dead weight and could never match lower-cased input.

2) [P0] ad_blockers over-reach: removed the generic protocol prefixes 'http://', 'https://', 'www.' (these matched almost any link at all, not specifically commercial ones) and removed academic file-sharing domains 'drive.google.com/', 'docs.google.com/', 'youtube.com/', 'dropbox.com/', 'onedrive.com/' — students routinely paste these when sharing lecture slides, assignment files, or reference videos, and because ad_blocker_trie is an early hard short-circuit to 'ignore' in analyze(), these entries were silently rejecting legitimate academic messages. ad_blockers now contains only messaging-app / social-discovery / URL-shortener domains, which are much stronger commercial-intent signals on their own.

3) [P0] Threshold mismatch: confidence_thresholds_design_target changed from the aspirational 0.78/0.55 pair (never enforced by runtime) to match config.py's actual CONFIDENCE_ACCEPT_THRESHOLD/CONFIDENCE_REVIEW_THRESHOLD defaults (0.65/0.40), so this file's documented tuning target matches what the engine genuinely applies. See the new design_principles note for the maintenance rule going forward.

4) [P1] Negation vs. implicit-distress conflict: 'ما عرفت احل', 'ما عرفت اسوي', 'ما فهمت شي', 'ما قدرت اخلص', 'ما لحقت اسوي' (and their base forms 'ما عرفت' / 'ما فهمت' / 'ما قدرت' / 'ما لحقت') were flagged as genuine student-help requests in request_phrases.indirect_distress, yet the pre_verb_negator 'ما' would trigger negation on the exact same text via _detect_negation(), suppressing the request's confidence. Added these phrases to negation.negation_exceptions so _detect_negation() correctly backs off when one of these failure-state phrases is present alongside the negator.

5) [P1] spam_categories / academic-context overlap: removed ambiguous standalone terms that can legitimately appear in academic requests and were previously hard-blocked via spam_trie's immediate 'ignore' short-circuit: 'تداول', 'اسهم', 'فوركس' from financial_spam (a finance/business student may legitimately ask for help with a report about these topics); 'ادويه' from irrelevant_commercial (overlaps with medical_documents/clinical_nursing academic terms); 'وظيفه', 'وظايف', 'عمل عن بعد', 'عمل من المنزل' from irrelevant_commercial (can appear in legitimate business/HR coursework requests). Kept the unambiguous job-ad phrase 'مطلوب موظفين', which has no plausible academic-request reading.

6) [P1] ignore_signals.health_general / medical academic overlap: 'مرض', 'علاج', 'دواء', 'مستشفي', 'طبيب', 'عنايه', 'صحه' removed from ignore_signals.health_general — these single tokens overlap heavily with academic_objects.medical_documents and academic_objects.clinical_nursing (nursing/medical students legitimately ask for help with 'بحث عن علاج مرض السكري', 'حاله دراسيه عن مريض', etc.) and, since ignore_signals is an early hard short-circuit in analyze(), were causing false rejections of legitimate academic health requests. Narrowed health_general to a small set of casual, clearly non-academic wellbeing chit-chat that is very unlikely to co-occur with a real academic object.

7) [P2] Lowered academic_objects.general_academic._weight_hint from 0.7 to 0.6 — this subsection (ماده/محاضره/جامعه/كليه/تخصص, etc.) is the most generic academic_objects category and the one most likely to appear in non-request chit-chat ('جامعة الملك سعود حلوة'), so it should contribute the least per-match weight of any academic_objects tier.

8) [P2] De-duplication: removed a duplicate 'يسلم' entry in templates.action (was listed twice) and a duplicate 'شخص' entry in templates.person (was listed twice). No semantic content removed — both canonical forms are still present exactly once.

9) [P2] Test suite expansion (audit item 33/34): grew test_cases from 21 total (10 positive / 9 negative / 2 borderline) to a much larger, scenario-driven set explicitly covering: negation-vs-distress, resolution+new-request-in-one-message, academic file-link messages, commercial-link messages, ambiguous finance/health academic topics, non-academic uses of intent verbs and template words, the 'احتاج دكتور' expert-ambiguity case, very short messages, and a long multi-clause message. See test_cases below.

templates._description: Word sets for template-based pattern generation. Engine combines them according to template_patterns at load time. Only 'need','person','action','expert','availability' are read by filter_engine.py v14.1's _generate_template_patterns(); 'urgency' is kept as a reserved/documented word bank for a future engine version that adds <urgency> tag support — it is NOT currently consumed by the generator. See design_principles for the known limitation that template_boost is not academic-context-gated at the engine level.

intent_verbs._description: Canonical first-person verb stems. Weighted for high precision. Intent alone (without an academic_object) is intentionally kept below the accept threshold via the scoring pipeline — see design_principles note on non-academic uses of these verbs (e.g. 'ادور على سكن').

implicit_request_patterns._note: Score only if academic object/context present

solve_actions._note: If 'حل' appears with technical_problem_terms, academic score for that object is halved

academic_objects._description: Specific academic items; enriched with high-precision terms.

negation._negation_exceptions_note: v15.2 fix: 'ما عرفت احل', 'ما فهمت شي', etc. are genuine failure-state help requests (also listed in request_phrases.indirect_distress) that happen to start with the pre_verb_negator 'ما'. Without these exceptions, _detect_negation() would treat them as a negated (i.e. suppressed) request. These entries make _detect_negation() correctly back off for that phrasing.

subject_markers._description: Comprehensive set of markers that identify the speaker as a student seeking help. IMPORTANT: these are CONTEXT signals only (feed the low-weight 'grammar_score' component, CFG.SCORE_WEIGHT_GRAMMAR=0.15 by default) — they are not, and must not be treated as, standalone intent signals. 'عندي سياره للبيع' contains 'عندي' but is not a help request.
subject_markers._note: Possessive suffixes (ي, نا) attached to academic objects are also detected via normalization.

provider_profile._rule: strong_provider/individual_provider + any commercial signal = immediate reject. weak_provider requires 3+ commercial signals.
provider_profile._false_positive_note: weak_provider verbs (نسوي/نساعد/نقدم...) are first-person-plural and can be used by a student describing a group project ('نسوي مشروع جماعي'), which is why weak_provider alone requires 3+ additional commercial signals rather than triggering on its own — do not lower that bar without re-testing against the group-project test cases below.

_ad_blockers_note: v15.2: scoped down from the previous list (see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 2). Read directly by filter_engine.py (self._ad_blockers = set(kw.get('ad_blockers', []))) — used both for the early ad_blocker_trie short-circuit in analyze() and as a +0.2 ad-score contribution in _detect_advertisement(). Removed: generic 'http://'/'https://'/'www.' prefixes (matched almost any link, not specifically commercial ones) and academic file-sharing domains 'drive.google.com/', 'docs.google.com/', 'youtube.com/', 'dropbox.com/', 'onedrive.com/' (students legitimately paste these when sharing lecture files / assignment briefs / reference videos). What remains are messaging-app / social-discovery / URL-shortener domains, which carry much stronger standalone commercial-intent signal.

spam_categories._v15_2_trim_note: Removed 'تداول'/'اسهم'/'فوركس' (financial_spam) — a business/finance student may legitimately request help with a report on these exact topics. Removed 'ادويه' (overlaps with medical_documents/clinical_nursing). Removed standalone 'وظيفه'/'وظائف'/'عمل عن بعد'/'عمل من المنزل' (can appear in legitimate HR/business coursework); kept 'مطلوب موظفين', which has no plausible academic-request reading. spam_trie is an early hard short-circuit to 'ignore' in analyze(), so ambiguous standalone terms here directly cause false negatives on legitimate academic requests — see fixes_changelog v15.2 item 5.

ignore_signals._health_general_v15_2_note: Trimmed from a broader list that previously included 'مرض'/'علاج'/'دواء'/'مستشفي'/'طبيب'/'عنايه'/'صحه' — those single tokens overlap heavily with academic_objects.medical_documents / academic_objects.clinical_nursing and were causing false 'ignore' rejections of legitimate nursing/medical-student academic requests (e.g. 'بحث عن علاج مرض السكري'). Kept only casual wellbeing chit-chat terms with essentially no academic-request reading. See fixes_changelog v15.2 item 6.

length_modifier._note: Keys use the 'X_to_Y' format filter_engine.py's _load_keyword_sets() parses (splits on '_to_'). Values intentionally do not penalize long academic messages: 11_to_30 stays at the neutral 1.0 ceiling, and even 31_to_9999 stays fairly close to neutral (0.9) rather than being treated as a quality signal in itself — length should only meaningfully discount very short (1-3 token) messages that lack enough context to disambiguate intent.

scoring_weights._note: Documentation of the DESIGN target weights. filter_engine.py v14.1 actually blends confidence using CFG.SCORE_WEIGHT_INTENT/ACADEMIC/GRAMMAR/DISTANCE/URGENCY/CONTEXT from config.py (env-overridable) as the single runtime source of truth. Keep these two in sync manually when re-tuning: current config.py defaults are intent=0.30, academic=0.25, grammar=0.15, distance=0.15, urgency=0.05, context=0.10.

negation_score.effect: multiplies base confidence by (1 - negation_score * 0.7), matching filter_engine.py's analyze()

advert_score.effect: multiplies base confidence by (1 - advert_score * 0.9), matching filter_engine.py's analyze()

explainability._note: reasons strings match the exact formats filter_engine.py's analyze() actually appends: 'intent_verb: X', 'academic_object: X', 'urgency: X', 'implicit_request', negation reasons, ad_detection reasons, 'template_boost: X'.

test_cases._note: text values are intentionally natural/raw Arabic (ة, hamzas, etc. as a real user would type) — they are run through the SAME normalization pipeline as production input, so pre-normalizing them here would test something other than real behavior. See _meta.design_principles. v15.2 significantly expands this suite (audit items 33/34) to explicitly cover negation-vs-distress, resolution+new-request, academic vs. commercial links, ambiguous finance/health topics, non-academic intent-verb/template uses, expert-word ambiguity, very short messages, and long messages.

high_confidence_boost_patterns._note: Curated static high-precision phrases, complementary to (not a replacement for) template_patterns' combinatorial generation. filter_engine.py's _load_keyword_sets() reads boost_data.get('patterns', []) from this section and unions it with the template-generated set into self._boost_patterns; a match adds +0.25 confidence and 'template_boost: X' to reasons. v15.2: all English tokens lower-cased ('PowerPoint'->'powerpoint', 'Excel'->'excel', 'Mind Map'->'mind map', 'Concept Map'->'concept map') — these were previously dead weight because filter_engine.py lower-cases input text but never lower-cases keyword entries (fixes_changelog v15.2 item 1).

_legacy_keys_note: The 9 keys directly above (request, advertisement, ignore, emoji_advertisement, education_providers, request_context, indirect_request, urgency, spam_patterns) are pre-v13 flat-list keys still present in config.py's _KW_CATEGORIES for backward compatibility. They are intentionally kept as EMPTY arrays rather than removed or left absent, so the schema contract stays fully visible instead of silently missing. Their function is fully covered by the structured v13+/v15 sections above (intent_verbs+request_phrases, advertisement_signals, ignore_signals, emoji_signals.ad_style_emoji, advertisement_signals.institution_terms, request_phrases/implicit_request_patterns, urgency_markers, spam_categories, respectively). Do not populate these unless a genuine need for the flat legacy format is identified — populating them would create a second, harder-to-maintain source of truth for data that already exists in the structured sections.
